h1: Occupational Driver's License (ODL) in El Paso, Texas
intro: A suspended Texas license does not have to mean losing your job. Under Transportation Code Chapter 521, Subchapter L, a court can grant an occupational driver's license that lets you drive to work, school and essential errands while the suspension runs. Attorney Robert Navar prepares and files the petition in El Paso County.
summary: An occupational driver's license (ODL) is a court-ordered restricted license for people whose Texas license is suspended for points, a DWI, or unpaid surcharges from before the 2019 repeal, allowing driving for work, school and household needs.
The ODL is obtained by filing a petition in the county or justice court, with an SR-22 insurance certificate; the judge's signed order then serves as your temporary license until DPS issues the card.
The order limits you to no more than 12 hours of driving per day and to the counties the judge approves (up to four), on the routes and schedule you ask for.
An ODL will not solve an OMNI hold or an expired license — those are fixed by clearing the tickets. We check which problem you actually have at a free consultation. Call 915-503-1600.

sections.heading: Who Qualifies for an Occupational License in Texas
paragraphs: Transportation Code Chapter 521, Subchapter L (521.241 and following) lets a court grant an occupational license to a person whose license has been suspended or revoked and who needs to drive for work, education or essential household duties. In El Paso the typical client has a suspension for too many points from moving-violation convictions, an administrative or court suspension after a DWI arrest, or an old Driver Responsibility Program surcharge default that was never resolved before the program was repealed in 2019.

Not every suspension qualifies. An ODL is generally not available when the license was suspended for a medical reason or for failure to pay child support, and some DWI histories carry statutory waiting periods. We review your DPS record at the consultation and tell you plainly whether an ODL is available and when.

One important distinction: a suspension is different from an OMNI hold. If DPS is refusing to renew your license because of unresolved tickets, you need the tickets cleared, not an ODL. If DPS has actively suspended your driving privilege, an ODL is the tool. Many clients have both, and we address them in the right order.

sections.heading: The ODL Petition: Where It's Filed and What Goes In It
paragraphs: An occupational license is granted by a court order, not by DPS. The petition is filed in a county court at law or a justice court in El Paso County — the Justice of the Peace precincts handle many of them — or, for a DWI-related suspension, often in the court that heard the criminal case. The petition is a sworn document that sets out why the suspension happened, why you need to drive, where you work or attend school, and the specific hours, days, routes and counties you are asking for.

Supporting documents matter. A letter from your employer confirming your schedule, a class schedule from UTEP or EPCC, and proof of insurance all strengthen the request. For Fort Bliss soldiers we include the duty schedule; for drivers who work across county lines we address that specifically, because the order only authorizes Texas counties.

Robert Navar drafts the petition and proposed order, files it, and sets it for the judge. In most El Paso courts a straightforward ODL petition is granted at a short hearing or on the papers, and we attend any hearing with you.

sections.heading: SR-22 Insurance and the Other Requirements
paragraphs: Before the judge signs, you must show financial responsibility with an SR-22 — a certificate your insurer files with DPS confirming you carry at least the state minimum liability coverage. Most carriers in El Paso can issue one within a day for a modest fee, and drivers who do not own a car can buy a non-owner SR-22 policy. The SR-22 must stay in force for the life of the occupational license; if it lapses, DPS cancels the ODL.

You will also need a certified copy of your driving record from DPS, any required DWI education or ignition interlock documentation when the suspension stems from a DWI, and payment of the court filing fee and the DPS license fee. We walk you through each item so the petition is complete the first time.

sections.heading: Hours, Routes and the Order You Carry
paragraphs: An occupational license is restricted by design. The statute caps driving at 12 hours in any 24-hour period, and the judge sets the days, times and purposes — typically work, school, medical appointments, church and essential errands like groceries and childcare. The order names the counties where you may drive, up to four, so an El Paso order can include neighboring counties if your work takes you there. DWI-related suspensions may carry additional conditions such as an interlock device.

Once the judge signs, we deliver the order to DPS along with the SR-22 and fee. The signed court order itself serves as your license until DPS issues the occupational license card, so you can drive the same day the order is signed. Keep a copy in the vehicle; if you are stopped, the officer will read the restrictions from it.

Driving outside the hours, counties or purposes in the order is treated like driving with no valid license, and it can lead to a driving while license invalid charge and revocation of the ODL. We write the order as broadly as your facts support.

sections.heading: Costs, Timeline and How the ODL Fits With Your Tickets
paragraphs: The total cost of an ODL has three parts: our attorney fee, quoted flat at the free consultation based on the type of suspension; the court filing fee; and the DPS occupational license fee. The SR-22 is paid to your insurer. In a routine points or surcharge case the process usually takes one to three weeks from first call to signed order, driven mostly by how fast the driving record and SR-22 arrive. DWI cases can take longer because of statutory waiting periods.

Most El Paso suspensions start with tickets, and that is where we can save you the most. If the convictions behind a points suspension are still pending, fighting them for a dismissal or deferred disposition may keep the suspension from growing. A DWLI or no driver's license ticket needs its own defense, which we handle for a flat $59–$69. Our free ticket and warrant lookup finds every open case first.

sections.heading: Getting Started on Your Occupational License
paragraphs: Bring your suspension notice or the letter from DPS, your insurance information and a rough list of the hours and places you need to drive. Call 915-503-1600 or contact us online; we serve El Paso, Horizon City, Socorro, Canutillo, Vinton, Anthony and Fort Bliss, and se habla español.
This page is general information, not legal advice about your case. Eligibility depends on your specific suspension, and we will tell you where you stand at the first conversation.

faqs.q: What is an occupational driver's license in Texas?
faqs.a: It is a restricted license authorized by Transportation Code Chapter 521, Subchapter L, granted by court order to a person whose regular license is suspended. It allows driving for work, school and essential household purposes within the hours, counties and conditions the judge sets.

faqs.q: Can I get an ODL for any suspension?
faqs.a: No. ODLs are commonly available for points suspensions, DWI-related suspensions and old surcharge defaults. They are generally not available for medical or child-support suspensions, and some DWI histories carry waiting periods. We review your DPS record before filing.

faqs.q: Do I need an SR-22 for an occupational license?
faqs.a: Yes. An SR-22 is a certificate of financial responsibility your insurer files with DPS. It must be in place before the judge signs the order and must stay active for the entire term of the ODL, or DPS will cancel the license.

faqs.q: How many hours a day can I drive on an ODL?
faqs.a: The statute limits an occupational license to no more than 12 hours in any 24-hour period. The judge sets the specific days, times and purposes, and the order can cover up to four counties. We draft the request to match your actual work and school schedule.

faqs.q: How long does it take to get an occupational license in El Paso?
faqs.a: In a routine points or surcharge case, usually one to three weeks from consultation to signed order, depending on how quickly the driving record and SR-22 arrive. The signed order lets you drive immediately while DPS prints the card.

faqs.q: DPS won't renew my license. Do I need an ODL?
faqs.a: Probably not. A renewal denial usually means an OMNI hold from unresolved tickets, which is fixed by clearing those cases, not by an ODL. See our OMNI hold removal page, or call us and we will tell you which problem you have.
